title: Consolidate scalar polynomial consumers under the native kernel
status: Source changes committed on main and fully locally qualified; cached rational-curve evaluation improves; remaining region regressions and completeness limits are explicit

change.implementation: Scalar consumers call Real::eval_poly directly; duplicate refinement sign evaluation calls the existing sign_at. The native exact-rational branch uses Rational multiply/add Horner, constructing only the final Real. Symbolic-coefficient handling, completed-square zero certificates, and the balanced nonrational-argument evaluator are unchanged.
test_changes: Local-field sign refinement certifies a directly represented nested quadratic root with symbolic leading scale at an included endpoint, and the monic midpoint case; both policies preserve ownership and exact payloads.

Coordinate-image regression covers empty and constant polynomials, zero/unit parameters, rational-parameter symbolic cancellation, a nested radical zero, and a degree-64 exact identity under both policies.
Existing rational polynomial degree/argument matrix now compares against an independent GMP power sum, not another Horner chain. No production GMP dependency is introduced.
contract_specific_evaluators_retained: Interval evaluation and simultaneous derivative evaluation, which have different contracts.

validation.scope: These results cover the exact source commits listed above. New concurrent rational-Bezier derivative-completeness edits observed before the checkpoint commit are preserved and are not covered by this qualification.

measurement_environment.dependency_control: Both sides retain the same frozen lower-stack sources. Hyperreal is d219a350462357af07d035fd316cba3b1cc339c9 plus the candidate's two-file patch; the concurrent Hypersolve quadratic-extraction change bb85085438e398b92ef56b0855332fc686403562 is excluded on both sides. Live qualification includes that change and the current Hyperreal conversion work.
measurement_environment.source_control: All eight changed source files matched the frozen candidate byte-for-byte. Both modified Hyperreal files also matched live HEAD before applying the patch. The two unchanged benchmark drivers and native evaluator baseline were hash-checked.
measurement_environment.quiet_sampling: No other build/test workers were present at either final comparison's start or at the broad comparison's end; intermediate bounded host process audit saw only the owned benchmark worker. No timing samples were excluded.

performance.decision: Keep the native consolidation for stronger exact certificates, substantial cached-evaluation improvements, and removal of duplicate machinery. Do not claim uniform speedups: the radial fixture and several retained-region rows regress and remain follow-up work.

extended_rational.interpretation: Use this longer matched run for cached-evaluation claims; the broad run's 64-control cached row has only 20 iterations.

rejected_intermediate.description: Direct consumer consolidation with the old native fused exact-rational evaluator was not kept as the final implementation. Longer runs confirmed cached-evaluation regressions of about 54.6% at 16 controls and 92.2% at 64 controls.

method_diagnostic.scope: Diagnostic timings compare three homogeneous-coordinate polynomial shapes across integer/fractional coefficients and three rational arguments; final acceptance uses the end-to-end curve measurements.

performance.storage_note: Each sample's row_nanoseconds array follows its fixture's median_rows order, which defines row names, iteration counts, and checksums. Compaction was verified lossless against the complete parsed results.

memory.scope: Small coupled-fiber fixture and four cold/cached evaluations of one 16-control rational curve. Heaptrack includes process startup and lifetime caches; reported end-live memory is not a leak diagnosis. These are not full slow-Boolean allocation profiles.
memory.decision: The final rational-curve control matches baseline allocation count and reported peak heap. The small fiber control uses 295 more allocations (+2.5%) and reports a slightly higher peak. Performance and certificate gains take precedence; no overall allocation reduction is claimed.

hyperreal_profile.scope: Unpaired four-iteration profile, including nonzero reported retention in five classes; not a leak-free or asymptotic memory-bound claim.

hypersolve_profile.reported_live_delta: zero in all reported workload rows

binary_sizes.decision: Region and rational benchmark executables shrink by 8,120 and 6,576 bytes. The test executable grows by 66,960 bytes with the new regression coverage; no universal binary-size reduction is claimed.

known_completeness_limit.status: Pre-existing and still reproduced on the final native kernel
known_completeness_limit.result: Old Horner cannot certify p(r)=0; the native evaluator can. Both remain undecided on p(m), although m-r is certified zero. Adding zero, distributing the half scale, or constructing the average with mul_add does not recover the missing certificate.
